newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NEW JOBLESS AND HOUSING FIGURES
The official jobless figure for February has increased to 8.8 percent, up point-two on the previous month.
The number of unemployed Australians is the highest it's been in two-and-a-half years, with 811,000 people searching for work.
During February the number of working Australians dropped by more than seven-thousand, and more than 24-thousand full time jobs disappeared.
The jobless rate has risen sharply in New South Wales and Tasmania, with Queensland the only state to record a drop.
Other figures released today show a marked pickup in the housing sector.
The number of houses financed in January rose by nine-point-three percent over the previous month, and the number of new dwellings purchased rose more than 12 per cent.
HOWARD RULES OUT KENNETT'S WORK-FOR-THE-DOLE SCHEME
The Prime Minister, John Howard, has ruled out Victoria setting up its own work-for-the-dole scheme.
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, says the Federal Government's scheme, offering part-time work on community projects, won't create real job skills.
He's proposed Victoria operate an alternative scheme, where young people are employed five days a week in a business environment.
Mr Howard says he welcomes Mr Kennett's contribution, and there may be scope for private sector involvement in the Federal scheme.
But he says he won't allow any state to offer work for the dole in a manner different to the rest of Australia.
FAMILY COURT CHIEF ON REMOVAL OF SERVICES
A Federal Government proposal to remove the Family Court's counselling and mediation services has received a mixed reaction from the court's Chief Justice.
Attorney General Darryl Williams flagged the possibility because of duplication with community organisations.
Chief Justice Alistair Nicholson says there is room for outside services, but the Family Court's service already resolves 60-per cent of cases before litigation starts.

Justice Nicholson says the move could provide relief on the Court's heavy work load, but he's concerned the Attorney General wrongly believes the Court has no role at all in dispute-resolution services.
He says the system in place at the moment is currently being looked to as a model for Singapore, Fiji and South Africa.
PRESSURE TO DESTROY SPECIAL BRANCH FILES
The New South Wales police service is under growing pressure to destroy many of the files held by the former Special Branch unit.
The unit was disbanded yesterday after revelations at the Police Royal Commission.
The Royal Commission's been told that Special Branch held files on lawyers, politicians and civil libertarians.
At last count the Special Branch had about 20-thousand active files.
Tim Anderson, who's at the centre of one of the unit's most embarassing cases has told ABC Radio he concerned that that sort of information should be made available to people, and then be destroyed.
Mr Anderson's calls have been backed up the President of the state's Bar Association, David Bennett.
PENALTY WATERED DOWN FOR DOLE BREACHERS
The Federal Government has confirmed it's watered down slightly the planned penalty for people who refuse to work for the dole or who breach social security rules.
The maximum penalty will still be the complete loss of unemployment benefits for 13 weeks, but it would be imposed for third and subsequent offences - rather than second offences.
The Senate rejected one set of penalties last December and the Government hopes the revised penalties will be accepted by the Senate.
Some welfare groups are prepared to back the new penalties.
SECOND HOAX CLAIMING ABORIGINALITY THIS MONTH
The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Arts Board says if Aboriginal writer Wanda Koolmatrie is not who she says she is, any profits made from the deception should be returned.
This follows reports today that Koolmatrie, author of the book, My Own Sweet Time, for which she received a 1995 Dobbie Award, is in fact white male writer Leon Carmen.
The apparent hoax follows revelations earlier this month, that acclaimed Aboriginal artist Eddie Burrup was really Elizabeth Durack.
Lydia Miller from the Arts Board has told ABC Radio that if the claims are true, the writer has acted deceitfully.
SCUD BEATS WOODY
Melbourne's Mark Philippoussis is through to the last 16 of the tennis Champions Cup in California with a 7-6, 7-6, win over compatriot Todd Woodbridge.
In a tournament upset, world number one Pete Sampras lost 6-7, 5-7, to Bohdan Ulihrach from the Check Republic.
Another Australian - Sandon Stolle lost 4-6, 4-6, to France's Cedric Pioline.
And Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic is also out in straight sets to Johnathon Stark from the U.S.
